title: 2013 AMC 10B Problem 11
statement: Real numbers \(x\) and \(y\) satisfy the equation \[x^2+y^2=10x-6y-34.\] What is \(x+y?\)

solutions.text:
This can be rewritten as \[x^2-10x+y^2+6y+34=0.\]

Completing the square yields \[x^2-10x+25+y^2+6y+9 \] \[=(x-5)^2+(y+3)^2\] \[=0.\] Since both squared terms are nonnegative and their sum is \(0,\) both must be \(0\). Thus \[(x-5)^2 = (y+3)^2=0.\]

Therefore, \(x=5,y=-3,\) so \(x+y=2.\)

Thus, the correct answer is B.
hints: Move all terms to one side and complete two squares
A sum of squares equals zero only when both squares are zero
